title: ZSDK Private Service Edges, groups, provisioning keys and enrollment
aliases: zsdk private service edge provisioning key

prose.text: {{publicly-accessible}} {{trusted-networks}} {{group-considerations}} Whether that requirement squares with disaster recovery being off by default is open {{gap:group-dr-requirement}}. The Publicly Accessible recommendations overlap for an edge with a public IP address {{gap:public-ip-recommendation}}, and the Client Connector wording is unconfirmed for ZSDK {{gap:client-connector-wording}}. Disaster recovery itself is in [[shared.zsdk.disaster-recovery]].

checks.do: Whether the Private Service Edge group's Publicly Accessible setting matches how users reach it, and whether the edge has a public IP address or a published IP set to a SNAT's public IP, where the recommendations overlap.
Whether the provisioning key has reached its utilization count, and whether the enrollment certificate has the same root as those used for App Connectors and Zscaler Client Connector.
Whether a Private Service Edge was cloned, since a clone's keys no longer match the virtual hardware fingerprints.

registration-and-purpose.statement: Private Service Edges register with the ZSDK cloud to download the policies and configuration they enforce, and manage the connections from App Connectors; they are used where Public Service Edges are not conveniently located between users and applications, or to keep application data traffic local for compliance.

quotes: Private Service Edges register with the ZSDK cloud, which allows them to download the relevant policies and configurations in order to enforce all policies.
Similar to Public Service Edges, Private Service Edges manage the connections from App Connectors.
Securely access applications when Public Service Edges in data centers are not conveniently located between users and the applications they need to reach.
Keep application data traffic local to help meet compliance and regulatory requirements.

distribution-forms.statement: Zscaler distributes Private Service Edge images for deployment in enterprise data centers and local private cloud environments (for example VMware).

quotes: Zscaler distributes images for deployment in enterprise data centers and local private cloud environments (e.g., VMware).

location-and-country-policy.statement: A user connecting to a Private Service Edge is located by its public IP address and the country-based policy for the mapped country is enforced; if the Private Service Edge group location is updated for an existing connection, the Public Service Edge uses the old location until its next new connection, and GeoIP configuration override is not supported for Private Service Edges.

quotes: After a user connects to a Private Service Edge, the user's location is determined by its public IP address, and then a country-based policy for the mapped country is enforced.
If the location of the Private Service Edge group is updated for an existing connection, the Public Service Edge uses the old location until the next time it makes a new connection.
Location changes via a GeoIP configuration override are not supported for Private Service Edges.

publish-and-listen-ips.statement: Publish IPs or Domains are what clients and App Connectors use to connect to the Private Service Edge, falling back to the Listen IPs if unspecified; with no Listen IPs configured the Private Service Edge listens on all interfaces.

quotes: If these are not specified, then the clients and App Connectors try to connect using the Listen IPs.
If this is not configured, then the Private Service Edge listens to all interfaces.
Publish IPs or Domains: The IP addresses and domains that clients and App Connectors can use to open a connection to the Private Service Edge.
Listen IPs: The IP addresses that the Private Service Edge listens for connection requests from clients and App Connectors at set addresses.

publish-ips-use-cases.statement: Publish IPs or domains are used mainly to name the ZSDK Private Cloud and find it through DNS, and second when the system uses a static external IP address (for example AWS) that is not part of the Private Service Edge.

quotes: The primary use case is to specify ZSDK Private Cloud by name and use a DNS to find it.
The second use case is if the Private Service Edge system is using a static external IP address (e.g., AWS)
because the IP address used by clients and App Connectors to connect to the Private Service Edge is not a part of the Private Service Edge.

undeployed-not-listed.statement: Added but undeployed Private Service Edges are not listed on the Private Service Edges page, which shows the last known public and private IP addresses of a disconnected one.

quotes: Added but undeployed Private Service Edges are not listed.
If the Private Service Edge was disconnected, the last known public IP address displays.
Private IP: The private IP address of the Private Service Edge. If the Private Service Edge was disconnected, the last known private IP address displays.

enrollment-process.statement: A Private Service Edge generates a hardware-fingerprint-encrypted private key and a CSR on first install, authenticates the CSR with its group's provisioning key, and receives a TLS client certificate pinned to its hardware fingerprint; once enrolled it is paired with a single customer account, cannot be enrolled again and must not be cloned.

quotes: the Private Service Edge must first generate the local private key, which it encrypts using a hardware fingerprint.
It uses the provisioning key assigned to its associated Private Service Edge group to authenticate the CSR to the ZSDK cloud.
The signed TLS client certificate is pinned to the Private Service Edge's hardware fingerprint.
After the Private Service Edge is enrolled, it is paired with a single customer account, and it cannot be enrolled again.
must not be cloned, because the keys will no longer match the virtual hardware fingerprints.
When a Private Service Edge is installed for the first time, it does not yet have a key pair
The Private Service Edge uses the local private key to generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR).

deployment-pairs.statement: Zscaler recommends deploying Private Service Edges in pairs for continuous availability during software upgrades, and the deployment article points to the ZPA Private Service Edge Deployment Prerequisites for sizing and platform requirements.

quotes: Zscaler recommends that Private Service Edges are deployed in pairs to ensure continuous availability during software upgrades.
read ZPA Private Service Edge Deployment Prerequisites, which provides detailed information on VM image sizing and scalability, supported platform requirements

signing-certificate.statement: The enrollment certificate for a Private Service Edge must have the same root certificate as the ones used to enroll App Connectors and Zscaler Client Connector; the preloaded certificates are Root, Client, Connector and Service Edge, and they are 2,048-bit RSA certificates supporting TLS 1.2 with cipher suite ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256.

quotes: must have the same root certificate that the enrollment certificate used for enrolling App Connectors and Zscaler Client Connector.
Service Edge: A signing certificate that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Private Service Edges.
These signing certificates are 2,048-bit key RSA certificates, which support TLS 1.2 connections (with cipher suite ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256).
Root: The root (i.e., parent) certificate for the Client or Connector signing certificates.
Client: A signing certificate that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connector.
Connector: A signing certificate that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connectors.

publicly-accessible.statement: Publicly Accessible determines whether the group's trusted network mapping is also available publicly to users outside those trusted networks. Zscaler recommends Enabled so remote users can reach the Private Service Edge over a public IP address, and Disabled when it has a public IP or a published IP set to the public IP of a SNAT such as a firewall; disabled without a trusted network, the nearest on-premises and roaming users are given its IP address, and the Private Service Edge should be reachable over a public IP address to avoid connectivity issues for remote users.

quotes: Publicly Accessible: Determines whether the Private Service Edge group's specific trusted network mapping is also available publicly for all users outside these trusted networks.
To mitigate connectivity issues for remote users who want to connect to this Private Service Edge, ensure that it is reachable over a public IP address.
Enabled: Zscaler recommends setting to Enabled to ensure the Private Service Edge is reachable over a public IP address if you need remote users to be able to connect to it.

Disabled: Zscaler recommends setting to Disabled if the Private Service Edge has a public IP address or a published IP address set to a public IP address of a Source Network Address Translation (SNAT) such as a firewall.

When Publicly Accessible is disabled without a trusted network, the IP address of the Private Service Edge is returned to the client for both on-premises and roaming users who are located closest to the Private Service Edge.

trusted-networks.statement: Client Connector Trusted Networks mapped to a Private Service Edge group are used to prioritize Private Service Edges when users connect from those networks.

quotes: Use this option to prioritize Private Service Edges matching the given trusted network when users connect from those trusted networks.
Client Connector Trusted Networks: Your organization's trusted networks that are mapped to the Private Service Edge group.

provisioning-key-purpose.statement: A Private Service Edge provisioning key is a text string generated when a ZSDK Private Service Edge is added; a prompt for it appears when deploying and it acts as an ID the ZSDK cloud uses to verify the Private Service Edge's authenticity, and it identifies the group the Private Service Edge must deploy to.

quotes: A provisioning key is a text string that is generated when you add a new ZSDK Private Service Edge.
When deploying a Private Service Edge, you are prompted to enter this provisioning key
which functions as an ID for the Private Service Edge
allows the ZSDK cloud to verify the Private Service Edge's authenticity and complete the deployment process
Each key is associated with a specific Private Service Edge group and identifies the group to which Private Service Edge must deploy.

provisioning-key-capabilities.statement: Private Service Edge provisioning keys let administrators deploy Private Service Edges into the associated group, limit how many times a key is used, view the key utilization count, edit the maximum number of uses and edit the signing certificate used to enroll Private Service Edge certificates.

quotes: Deploy Private Service Edges into an associated Private Service Edge group.
Limit the number of times a key is used for deployment.
View the current key utilization count.
Edit the maximum number of key uses.
Edit the signing certificate used to enroll Private Service Edge certificates.

provisioning-key-exhaustion.statement: A Private Service Edge provisioning key is generated with a specified number of times it can be used to deploy Private Service Edges; ZSDK displays the number of times a key is used on the Private Service Edge Provisioning Keys page, and once a key is used the maximum number of times, an administrator can instead associate multiple provisioning keys to a single Private Service Edge group.

quotes: When you generate a provisioning key, you specify the number of times it can be used to deploy Private Service Edges.
ZSDK tracks the number of times a key is used to deploy a Private Service Edge and displays the number on the Private Service Edge Provisioning Keys page.
After a key is used the maximum number of times, you can edit the maximum number of times a key is used or associate multiple provisioning keys to a single Private Service Edge group.

provisioning-keys-page-columns.statement: The Private Service Edge Provisioning Keys page lists, per key, Name, Maximum # of Private Service Edges, Provisioning Key Utilization Count, Private Service Edge Group and the copyable Provisioning Key; no filters are applied by default and a key can be downloaded in TXT format.

quotes: Name: The name of the Private Service Edge provisioning key.
Maximum # of Private Service Edges: The maximum number of Private Service Edges that can be deployed using the key.
Provisioning Key Utilization Count: The number of times the provisioning key has been used.
Private Service Edge Group: The Private Service Edge group associated with the key.
Provisioning Key: The key needed for deploying a Private Service Edge. You can copy the provisioning key.
By default, no filters are applied.
Download the provisioning key in a TXT format.

provisioning-key-naming.statement: A Private Service Edge provisioning key name becomes the prefix of each Private Service Edge enrolled with it, with the nth enrollment numbered (AWS Oregon-1, AWS Oregon-2).

quotes: This name is automatically assigned as a prefix to the name of each Private Service Edge enrolled with it.
if you enter AWS Oregon as a provisioning key name in this step, the first Private Service Edge you enroll with this key is named AWS Oregon-1.
This number signifies that it is the nth Private Service Edge to be enrolled with the key.
The next Private Service Edge you enroll with the same key is named AWS Oregon-2, and so on.

provisioning-key-rules.statement: A Private Service Edge provisioning key is unique to each group, has a maximum reuse count that can be modified after the Private Service Edge is added, and cannot be copied once its utilization count is reached; the signing certificate signs all Private Service Edges deployed with the key.

quotes: Each provisioning key is unique to each Private Service Edge group.
After adding the Private Service Edge, this number can be modified.
If the Provisioning Key Utilization Count is reached, you cannot copy the key.
All Private Service Edges deployed with this key have their certificates signed with this signing certificate.
Maximum Reuse of Provisioning Key: Enter the maximum number of instances where this key can be used to enroll a Private Service Edge.

group-considerations.statement: The Private Service Edge groups article says groups require disaster recovery to be enabled to ensure business continuity, and that a new group is not needed for every added Private Service Edge.

quotes: Private Service Edge groups require disaster recovery to be enabled to ensure business continuity.
You do not need to create a new Private Service Edge group every time you add a Private Service Edge.

release-history.statement: Release notes date ZSDK Private Service Edges and disaster recovery to April 15, 2025, when Disaster Recovery could be enabled for a Private Service Edge group.

quotes: April 15, 2025
When configuring a ZSDK Private Service Edge, you can enable Disaster Recovery for a ZSDK Private Service Edge group.

group-dr-requirement.title: Whether a Private Service Edge group must have disaster recovery enabled
group-dr-requirement.detail: The Private Service Edge groups article says groups require disaster recovery to be enabled to ensure business continuity, while the Private Service Edge article says disaster recovery is disabled by default for groups designated for it. The captured pages do not reconcile the two.

public-ip-recommendation.title: How Publicly Accessible Enabled relates to a Private Service Edge that has a public IP address
public-ip-recommendation.detail: The Enabled recommendation is for a Private Service Edge reachable over a public IP address, while the Disabled recommendation is for one that has a public IP address or a published IP set to a SNAT's public IP. The captured pages do not say which setting applies to an edge with a public IP that remote users reach.
public-ip-recommendation.blocks: answering which Publicly Accessible setting a Private Service Edge with a public IP address should use

client-connector-wording.title: Which client the Zscaler Client Connector wording on Trusted Networks and signing certificates refers to
client-connector-wording.detail: The Client Connector Trusted Networks field and the Client and Connector signing certificates name Zscaler Client Connector, while the rest of the ZSDK pages refer to the ZSDK client and the hub separates ZSDK from Client Connector. No captured page says whether these apply to the ZSDK client.
